$description: The New Project wizard: two steps in one dialog. Step 1 asks where the site comes from — a starter gallery that ends with one Start from scratch card, an Import of a site that already exists, or an Agent brief — and step 2 asks what it is called and where it is written. A `jx-dialog`, so the platform owns modality, Escape, focus restoration and the backdrop, which is what retired the fixed `.new-project-modal` card, the `<sp-underlay>` beside it, the `z-index: 1000` that card needed to climb back out from under its own scrim, and the hand-drawn header with its own close button. The footer is the dialog's too: Cancel, Back and the primary are `cancelLabel`, `secondaryLabel` and `confirmLabel`, so the wizard says which answers exist by naming them rather than by drawing three buttons per step. Nothing here knows what a starter is, which platform writes to a repository rather than a folder, what makes an AI gate open, or how a breakpoint policy is spelled — `new-project/new-project-modal.ts` keeps the flow, `new-project/import-tab.ts` the brief and `new-project/location-fields.ts` the destination, and all three hand over strings, flags and one discriminant per branch. The three AI controllers are islands: their own mounted documents, placed by the adapter into boxes this document renders empty (§9.4).

style.$description: Forty-three `.new-project-*` rules in `styles/overlays.css` become the parts below, and eight of them do not travel. `.new-project-modal` was a fixed, centred, bordered, shadowed card with its own width and `z-index: 1000`, and a modal `<dialog>` is every one of those; `.new-project-modal-header`, `.new-project-modal-title`, `.new-project-modal-body` and `.new-project-modal-footer` are the header, headline, scroll body and button row `jx-dialog` already draws; `.new-project-tabs` drew a rule under the strip that `jx-tabs` draws itself; `.new-project-error--global` pinned the backend error outside the scroll body, which a dialog that scrolls as one has nowhere to put; and `.new-project-field` / `.new-project-label` drew a label above a control, which is `jx-field` with `span` — with the label actually NAMING the control, which a bare `<span>` beside a textfield never did. Three repairs travel with the rest. Every `--spectrum-font-size-*` reference is gone: those names resolve only inside `<sp-theme>` and a document mounted in the dialog layer is outside it, so all eleven would silently have taken their hard-coded fallback. `var(--accent, #3b82f6)` on the selected card loses the hex, which was the same bug written the other way round. And the two thumbnail wells read `var(--bg-elevated, #1a1a1a)` for a token no stylesheet in this package defines, so the fallback was not a fallback — it was the value; they take `--bg-input`, which is the recessed surface the rest of the chrome uses.

& [part=\"blurb\"].$description: The sentence at the top of a source tab: what this path does, before any field asks for anything. `blurb` rather than `intro`, and the footnote below is `footnote` rather than `note`, because the three AI controllers mount their own documents INSIDE this one: `surfaces/ai-managed-connect.json` draws a `[part="intro"]` and `surfaces/ai-credentials-form.json` a `[part="note"]`, and a scoped rule on either name would restyle a surface this document does not own.

& [part=\"card\"].$description: A whole card is the button, because the answer is the starter rather than a control inside it. `font: inherit` because a `<button>` does not inherit type, and what it inherits here is the dialog's own body size rather than a number this surface picked.

&[data-art=\"blank\"].$description: The one non-starter card, last in the gallery and spanning it, so the sites lead.

& [part=\"creds\"].$description: The gate's column: the keyless offer above the key form, both of them mounted documents of their own. `max-width` so three text fields do not stretch to the width of a large dialog.

& [part=\"managed-island\"], & [part=\"c.$description: An island's box lays nothing out: each controller's own host is `display: contents`, so what the column above sees is the mounted document's own root and not a wrapper that would become the flex item in its place.

& [part=\"breakpoints\"].$description: A mode picker, whichever value control that mode takes, and the rounding rule. It wraps rather than scrolls — the widths field is the one that needs room, and it should get it.

& [part=\"location-row-controls\"].$description: The Location field takes the slack; Browse… stays its natural width.

& [part=\"url\"], & [part=\"prompt\"], &.$description: The kit's fields are `inline-flex`, which is right in a row of controls and wrong for the one control of a `span` row. Named one by one rather than as `& jx-textfield`, because the credentials island below is three more text fields in the same tree and none of them is this document's to size.

& [part=\"context\"].$description: WHICH source this project is being made from, said on the step that no longer shows the tab strip.

& [part=\"destination-preview\"].$description: Live preview of where the project will land — the answer to “where did that go?”.

& [part=\"name-failure\"], & [part=\"des.$description: Four refusals, one look, and none of them called `error`: `jx-textfield` and `jx-field` both draw a `[part="error"]` of their own inside this same tree, and the kit is light DOM, so a scoped rule on that name would restyle every field's own error line.

& [part=\"failure\"].$description: The backend's refusal, said at the end of the body so it sits directly above the footer the reader is about to press again. It used to be pinned outside the scroll box; a dialog scrolls as one, so what replaces the pin is being last.

children.textContent: Every starter is a complete site copied in as plain files you own — open it, look at it, then make it yours.

children.$description: Where `ui/ai-managed-connect.ts`'s own mounted document goes. The node is rendered EMPTY and the adapter puts the controller's host inside it — the one seam a foreign mount may arrive through (specs/studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4). It is drawn even when the platform brokers nothing, because the controller answers that question itself and hands back nothing to place.

Where `ui/ai-credentials-form.ts`'s own mounted document goes. Three fields a reader is typing into, so it must survive every repaint of the wizard around it: the document renders this box and never its contents, and the adapter places the same host node back into it rather than rebuilding one.

children.textContent: Describe the site you want; the assistant builds it in the editor while you watch.

$props.label: Minimum fidelity
$props.description: Below this average, the assistant reports that the clone did not match the original. A floor rather than a target: a faithful import of a complicated site still lands well under 100. Set 0 to report the score without judging it.

children.$description: Where `ui/ai-model-picker.ts`'s own mounted document goes. The picker holds the in-flight catalogue fetch and the credentials the last failure belonged to, so it is one controller for the life of the wizard and this box is only ever where its host is put.

$props.label: What should the assistant do with it?

$props.placeholder: Keep the layout but modernise the typography, and turn the news list into a content collection…
